Modified read: The statement points to solid ongoing growth and a low unemployment rate while acknowledging inflation remains somewhat elevated and uncertainty still elevated. Policy stays restrictive—target range held at 4.25–4.5% with continued balance‑sheet runoff and interest on reserve balances at 4.4%—and guidance remains data‑dependent.

Financial Stability Report overlay (April 11, 2025) tempers the macro-positive tone: vulnerabilities persist in commercial real estate exposures, nonbank run‑prone funding (prime MMFs, stablecoins), and pockets of household credit stress (e.g., rising auto‑loan delinquencies), alongside periodic Treasury market liquidity strains. At the same time, the banking system’s capital and liquidity remain solid, and core funding markets continue to function. Net effect: a cautiously hawkish, risk‑managed stance—slightly positive on activity but more muted once financial‑stability risks are considered.

Adjusted sentiment: slightly positive, reduced to reflect FSR‑highlighted vulnerabilities.
